question: Should I Require an Account or Allow Guest Checkout?
metaDescription: Guest checkout generally converts better — requiring an account upfront is one of the most common, well-documented causes of cart abandonment.
shortAnswer: Allowing guest checkout, with account creation offered as an optional, low-friction step (or automatic afterward), consistently outperforms requiring an account upfront — forcing registration before purchase is one of the most well-documented, avoidable causes of checkout abandonment across ecommerce generally, not just WooCommerce specifically. There are narrow exceptions (a members-only store, a B2B platform requiring approved accounts) where requiring an account is a deliberate, justified choice.

bodyHtml:
Why Guest Checkout Wins in Most Cases

Requiring an account adds a real, immediate barrier at exactly the moment a customer is deciding whether to complete a purchase — asking them to create a password, verify an email, or fill in extra fields before they've even paid introduces friction with no immediate benefit to them. Guest checkout removes that barrier while WooCommerce still captures the order and customer details normally; account creation can be offered afterward as a simple one-click option once the purchase is already secured.

When Requiring an Account Actually Makes Sense

  • A membership or subscription-based store where an account is inherently required to access the ongoing service being purchased, not an arbitrary gate on a one-time purchase.
  • A B2B/wholesale platform with approved-account pricing or terms, where account status genuinely determines what a customer can see or buy in the first place.
  • A store with a strong repeat-purchase pattern might see a smaller conversion penalty from requiring accounts, since existing customers are already registered — though new customer acquisition still suffers the same friction.
  • Fraud prevention is sometimes cited as a reason to require accounts, but this is generally better handled through payment gateway fraud tools and order review processes than by gating checkout itself.

Setting Up Guest Checkout Well

  1. Enable guest checkout under WooCommerce → Settings → Accounts & Privacy if not already active.
  2. Offer optional account creation at checkout with a simple checkbox, rather than a separate required step.
  3. Consider automatic account creation from guest order data post-purchase (a common pattern), letting customers set a password later via email if they want ongoing access, without blocking the original purchase.
  4. Test actual conversion impact if the store currently requires accounts, since this is one of the more measurable, evidence-backed checkout changes available.
